subject: Finova: Performance SLOs & Multi-region Routing (follow-up)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@finova.com>
Cc: Carlos Mendez <carlos.mendez@finova.com>
Date: Tue, 03 Nov 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Finova — Post-call recap & next steps (performance / routing)

Hi Lena / Carlos,

Thanks again for the 30-minute call today — great discussion and appreciate the clarity on your latency and routing priorities. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can align the technical follow-up: 

Recap:
- Primary workload: customer-facing conversational assistant (multi-utterance, streaming) integrated into Finova web and mobile apps.
- Current traffic estimate: steady-state ~120 reqs/s, peak ~400 reqs/s.
- Target SLOs you mentioned: p95 end-to-end generation latency <= 500ms for short prompts (<=128 tokens); p50 ideally < 200ms.
- Concurrency: expected 1k+ concurrent sessions across regions at peak.
- Streaming requirement: yes — real-time token streaming to client (websocket).
- Data residency: EU data must remain in EU regions; US traffic can stay in US. APAC is future expansion — prefer multi-region routing with regional KV/residency for EU requests.

Questions / clarifications we need to confirm before the demo perf run:
1) Can you confirm the p95 500ms SLO applies to median-response prompts (~<128 tokens) or to longer generation windows?
2) For peak concurrency, is 1k+ concurrent sessions per-region or global?
3) Any hard constraints on TTFB (time to first byte) versus full completion latency?

Next steps I propose:
- Aditya (cc'd) will scope a short perf test targeting US and EU regions based on your numbers.
- We'll share a draft SLA & regional routing diagram for your infra team to review (attaching SLA-draft + routing diagram).
- Schedule a 45-min technical deep-dive next week to validate model variants, batching/quantization options, and streaming behaviour.

Would Mon/Tue next week at 10am PT / 1pm ET work for you for the deep-dive? If you prefer a different time, tell us what works.

Thanks — we'll keep this tight and focused on validating whether we meet the p95 / streaming constraints you care about.

Best,
Marissa
Marissa Cole | Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0132
Redwood Inference

From: Carlos Mendez <carlos.mendez@finova.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@finova.com>
Date: Thu, 05 Nov 2026 09:30:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Finova — Post-call recap & next steps (performance / routing)

Thanks Marissa — this looks good. A couple of clarifications from our side: 

- The p95 <= 500ms target applies to our common short-turn prompts (authentication checks, single-turn clarification prompts) — typically <=128 tokens total. For long-form generation (>512 tokens) we can tolerate higher p95 but would like reasonable TTFB for streaming.
- Concurrency: 1k+ concurrent sessions is a global number, but at peak we expect ~400 concurrent sessions in EU and ~500 in US, with remainder in APAC.
- Streaming: critical. We need token-level streaming (WebSocket) with TTFB for first token ideally < 200ms in the target region.
- Data residency: EU-origin requests and any PII must be processed and stored only in EU. We will need a runbook or documentation to confirm residency for audit.

Also, we will need SOC2-type evidence and a high-level SLA for procurement to start internal conversations.

Mon/Tue morning works for a deep-dive — Mon 10am PT would overlap poorly with EU. Would Tue 10am PT / 19:00 CET work? If that's tight for you, propose alternatives.

Thanks,
Carlos
Carlos Mendez | Head of Platform Integrations, Finova
carlos.mendez@finova.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Carlos Mendez <carlos.mendez@finova.com>, Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@finova.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 06 Nov 2026 08:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Finova — Post-call recap & next steps (performance / routing)

Carlos — perfect, thanks for the detail. Quick answers inline and next steps: 

- p95 SLO scope: confirmed — we'll target p95 <= 500ms for common short prompts (~<=128 tokens). For >512 tokens we'll focus on TTFB and streaming cadence rather than end-to-end completion time.
- Concurrency: noted — we'll configure the perf test to mirror ~400 EU / ~500 US concurrency and a small APAC sample.
- Streaming / TTFB: we can run tests to validate first-token TTFB < 200ms in-region. Our runtime supports real-time token streaming over websockets and HTTP chunked streaming; we'll capture TTFB and per-token latencies in the results.
- Data residency: Redwood Private / Dedicated options support regionally pinned processing and storage (EU-only). We will provide documentation and a runbook showing data flow and KMS integration for EU keys. Aditya will provide SOC2 artifacts and the procurement-facing SLA.

Attachments: I attached the SLA draft and a regional-routing diagram showing our routing/fallback tiers (primary region, cross-region fallback, and model-variant fallbacks).

Action items:
1) Aditya — scope perf harness (US + EU) and share test plan + required creds for a short redwood-perf test. Please include token sizes and model variant (we recommend starting with rwd-medium-quant for cost/perf) and config for streaming.
2) Marcus — can you prep a short checklist of quantization/model trade-offs we should call out in the deep-dive?
3) Carlos / Lena — confirm Tue 10am PT / 19:00 CET for the deep-dive or propose an alternate time.

Proposed calendar: Tue, Nov 10, 2026 — 10:00am PT / 19:00 CET (45m).

Thanks all — we'll be ready to run the perf window as soon as we get confirmation.

Cheers,
Marissa

Hi Carlos / Lena — Aditya here (solutions engineering). I'll own the perf test and run a short validation window next week. Planned scope: 

- Regions: us-west1 (US), europe-west1 (EU). Small APAC run in asia-southeast1 to sanity-check routing.
- Workload: streaming conversational workload, average prompt size 80 tokens, max 512 tokens.
- Targets: p95 <= 500ms for short prompts; first-token TTFB < 200ms in-region.
- Concurrency config: 500 concurrent sessions US, 400 concurrent sessions EU, 100 global throttled to APAC sample.
- Model: rwd-medium-quant (start), rwd-large-quant (if we need better quality).
- Measurement: per-request p50/p95/p99, TTFB, per-token latencies, and peak throughput sustained for 5 minutes.

Reqs for test: 
- A short API key or a test account (we can use our test runner against a sandbox project you provide, or do a secure shared perf run on Redwood Dedicated with EU pinning).
- A sample prompt set (5-10 representative prompts). If you want us to use anonymized production prompts, we can sign an NDA — otherwise we'll use synthetic prompts matching length/profile.

I'll prepare a one-page test plan and share it by EOD Monday. Per Marissa's note, I'll include SOC2 artifacts and the procurement-facing SLA (attached).

Tue 10am PT / 19:00 CET works for me — I'll send the invite after we confirm.

—Aditya
